content: Recently, BIBREF0 introduced LAMA (LAnguage Model Analysis) to investigate to what extent pretrained language models have the capacity to recall factual knowledge without the use of fine-tuning. The training objective of pretrained language models is to predict masked tokens in a sequence. With this “fill-in-the-blank” scheme, question answering tasks can be reformulated as cloze statements. For example, “Who developed the theory of relativity?” is reformulated as “The theory of relativity was developed by [MASK].”. This setup allows for unsupervised open domain question answering. BIBREF0 find that, on this task, pretrained language models outperform supervised baselines using traditional knowledge bases with access to oracle knowledge.
